title: The key, the room, the stairs
goal: Master the one thing that makes Bulgarian truly unique among all the Slavic languages: a definite article that sticks to the **end** of the noun, in three genders and the plural.
bekal: attach the definite article to masculine, feminine, neuter and plural nouns
tell the long form **-ът** from the short form **-а**
read the masculine ending -а correctly as *-ă*
ask where things are in a hotel
recognize when the article is NOT used

dialogs.title: Диалог — Hotel reception in Sofia
dialogs.intro: Ani arrives at her hotel. Watch the ending of every noun in this dialogue — almost all of them carry a definite article stuck on the back, and its shape keeps changing.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: Good afternoon! I have a reservation.

lines.speaker: Рецепционист:
lines.id: Thank you. Your room is number twelve. Here's the key.
lines.literal: thank-you. room-the — your — is — number — twelve. here-is — key-the.

lines.speaker: Рецепционист:
lines.id: The elevator is over there, on the right. But it's not working today.
lines.literal: elevator-the — is — there, on-the-right. but — today — not — works.

lines.speaker: Рецепционист:
lines.id: The stairs are on the left. The room is on the second floor.
lines.literal: stairs-the — are — on-the-left. room-the — is — on — second-the — floor.

lines.speaker: Рецепционист:
lines.id: Breakfast is from seven to ten, in the restaurant downstairs.
lines.literal: breakfast-the — is — from — seven — to — ten, in — restaurant-the — downstairs.

notes: **Bulgarian sticks its article on the END of the word.** *Стая* = room; *стаята* = the room. *Ключ* = key; *ключът* = the key. There's no separate word like *the* or *der*. Think of it as English "the" moved to the back and glued on: "room-the". That's exactly how the literal lines in this course show it.

**Bulgarian is the only Slavic language with a definite article** (along with its close neighbor Macedonian). Russian, Polish, Czech, Croatian — none of them has one. If you've read that "Slavic languages have no articles", that's true of all of them except the one you're learning.

⚠️ **Паспорта is pronounced *pas-POR-tă*, not *pas-POR-ta*.** The short masculine ending is written with the letter **а** but always pronounced **ă** — the *u* sound in *but*. The same goes for *ключа* (*KLYOO-chă*) and *ресторанта* (*res-to-RAN-tă*). This is the only place where Bulgarian spelling truly lies; once you're used to it, there are no more surprises.
**Ето means "here is / here you are", said while handing something over.** It isn't a verb and doesn't need *е*. *Ето ключа* — here's the key. *Ето ме* — here I am.
**Стълбите is plural, and Bulgarian treats it as plural** — just like English "the stairs". So the verb is *са*, not *е*.

**На втория етаж — "on the second floor".** Ordinal numbers take the article too, and it sticks to the number, not to *етаж*. Unit 12 explains the rule; for now learn the chunk: *на първия / втория / третия етаж*. (Bulgarians count floors like Americans: the ground floor is the first.)
**От … до … — "from … to/until …"**, used for both time and place. *От седем до десет* (from seven to ten), *от София до Пловдив* (from Sofia to Plovdiv).

**Не работи means both "isn't working" and "doesn't work (at a job)".** Signs saying *Не работи* hang on elevators, ATMs and doors all over Bulgaria — read: "out of order". These may be the two most useful words you can recognize on day one.

grammars.title: The definite article — four basic forms
body: All you need to look at is the last letter of the noun. There's nothing to memorize beyond the rows below.
after: Notice the sound pattern: feminine and neuter use **-та / -то**, plurals use **-те / -та**. They're all built on the letter **т**. Only masculine singular uses **ъ**, and only masculine singular has two forms.

grammars.title: Long form vs short form — masculine singular only
body: Masculine nouns have two article forms, and the choice depends on **the word's role in the sentence**. It's the last remnant of the case system Bulgarian threw away.
after: Quick test: **replace the word with "he/him".** If the sentence works with *той* ("he", the subject), use the long form. If it has to be *него* ("him", the object), use the short form.

⚠️ In everyday speech most Bulgarians use the short form for everything. The long/short rule is a rule of **writing**, and breaking it in speech is almost never noticed. Don't let it stop you mid-sentence; write it correctly, speak it fluently.

sections.title: When to use the article — and when not to

blocks.text: When in doubt, the question is always the same: **does the person I'm talking to know which thing I mean?** If yes, add the article. If not, leave the word bare.

head: Use the article when…
Example
Meaning
rows: the thing has already been mentioned
I have a room. The room is small.
it's clear to both sides which one
there's only one in the world
you're talking about a category in general

head: DON'T use the article when…
Example
Meaning
rows: the thing is just being introduced

blocks.text: ⚠️ The fourth row matters and beginners break it often: **има** and **няма** introduce something new, so the noun can't be definite yet. *Има ресторант* = there's a restaurant. *Ресторантът е там* = the restaurant is over there. Unit 4 is all about this pair of words. Note also the last row of the first table: Bulgarian uses the article for general statements ("coffee-the is expensive") where English uses none.

sections.title: Eye training: twenty words, bare and with the article

blocks.text: Read down the list, out loud. Cover the right-hand columns, guess the form with the article, then check. This five-minute drill replaces half an hour of memorizing rules.

Look at *водата* (*vo-da-TA*) and *децата* (*deh-tsa-TA*): in some words **the stress moves onto the article**. There aren't many, and this course always prints the pronunciation, so just learn the ones you meet.

exercises.prompt: Add the definite article. For masculine nouns write the LONG form.
Choose the right masculine form: long or short.
Put the words in the right order.

items: The stairs are on the left.
Breakfast is from seven to ten.

answers: книгата — градът — млякото — стълбите — вечерта — детето
Асансьорът е там. — Стаята е на втория етаж. — Стълбите са наляво. — Закуската е от седем. — Ресторантът е долу.
Къде е стаята? — Ето ключа. — Градът е много хубав. — Стълбите са наляво. — Закуската е от седем до десет.
